an10.28:5.1: ‘Two things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said,
an10.28:5.2: but why did he say it?
an10.28:5.3: Becoming completely disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed regarding two things, seeing their limits and fully comprehending their meaning, a mendicant makes an end of suffering in this very life.
an10.28:5.8: Becoming completely disillusioned, dispassionate, and freed regarding these three things, seeing their limits and fully comprehending their meaning, a mendicant makes an end of suffering in this very life.
an10.28:5.9: ‘Three things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said, and this is why he said it.
an10.28:6.1: ‘Four things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said,
an10.28:6.2: but why did he say it?
an10.28:6.7: ‘Four things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said, and this is why he said it.
an10.28:7.1: ‘Five things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said,
an10.28:7.2: but why did he say it?
an10.28:7.3: Becoming well developed in five things—seeing their limits and fully fathoming their meaning—a mendicant makes an end of suffering in this very life.
an10.28:7.12: With a mind well developed in these eight things—seeing their limits and fully fathoming their meaning—a mendicant makes an end of suffering in this very life.
an10.28:7.13: ‘Eight things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said, and this is why he said it.
an10.28:8.1: ‘Nine things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said,
an10.28:8.2: but why did he say it?
an10.28:8.7: ‘Nine things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That’s what the Buddha said, and this is why he said it.
an10.28:10.2: ‘One thing: question, summary recital, and answer. …
an10.28:10.3: Ten things: question, summary recital, and answer.’ That is how I understand in detail the meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.
